decisions.reason: “Ruuuuumble!” fits the rumbling sound effect.
It preserves the heat and the hundreds-of-meters span in natural prose.
It keeps the lava-covered deathscape and the two figures standing above it.
“Half-gray-haired” preserves 반백 more precisely than “gray-haired.”
The glossary requires “monster,” and “charred” preserves the source’s burned condition.
“You’re a tough bastard” keeps the blunt, profane voice and sense.
“He could not” naturally completes the forceful repetition.
It preserves the one remaining hand and the firm grip.
It keeps the transformation from a short, slender staff to a longer, thicker one.
It preserves the weapon’s history and the title it earned its master.
SOL drops the muttering cue in 뇌까렸다.
“Old. Man!” conveys the insult in the source’s broken-out delivery.
The mist still stirs like a living thing and shoots toward Kim Hwajong.
“Crush it” preserves the source’s sense of breaking apart.
The observation is carried into H016, so deleting this duplicate avoids repetition.
It retains the mist closing in and the staff striking the ground.
It preserves the spreading wave and the ring of flames around him.
The mist still touches the flames and crumbles away like ash.
SOL drops the image of the human standing tall in the monster’s eyes.
“It” refers clearly to the unexpected situation.
It keeps both the wound and the nullified attack.
SOL changes the monster’s address “You, human!” into the assertion “You are human!”
It preserves the Fear-filled roar and Kim Hwajong’s calm heart.
“Misjudged one thing” keeps the mistaken assumption in natural phrasing.
“Not now” adds a temporal limit absent from the source’s claim that he has no fear.
It keeps the unreachable words, faint smile, and his fear moving away.
SOL changes the condition “could survive” to the fact “survived.”
It preserves the possible deaths and the willingness to be reduced to ash.
“With a glad heart” keeps the joy behind his grip.
It preserves mana surging into the weapon and erupting as flame.
“Sweep it away” fits the command to carry the target off.
It retains the brief incantation and the advancing wave of fire.
It keeps the trunk’s elephant-like shape and enormous scale.
It preserves the wind overwhelming the fire and the wind blades raking the area.
It keeps the paper-like destruction and his narrow escape.
SOL drops the low voice specified by the source.
“Beneath his foot” changes the source’s flame bursting along the tip of his planted foot.
It retains his explosive forward movement and the shadow overhead.
The shorter ellipsis preserves the startled pause.
It keeps instinct beating reason and the layered shields forming above him.
The pressure still crushes the overlapping shields in the next instant.
“They” clearly refers to the shields and preserves their shattering.
It preserves the overwhelming force, magical power, broken shields, and shaken mana.
Removing “between” does not change where the blood sprays from.
It preserves the blurred vision and his desperate evasive movement.
“Defensive spell” naturally conveys the magic that buys him time.
It keeps the near miss, ground impact, and fragments scraping his calf.
SOL drops the explicit contrast that he smiles instead of groaning.
It preserves the staff’s heat and the swelling sphere of flame.
The source does not specify a mouthful; “coughed up blood” keeps the action.
“Burst. Barrage of fire” preserves the command and image without a stiff calque.
It keeps the dazzling light-flames bursting as the spell completes.
The glossary requires “monster”; SOL also replaces that category with the name Behemoth.
The cry is still swallowed by a blast that shakes the area.
SOL drops the physical detail that the fire sweeps through the inside of the legs.
It keeps the agony and charcoal-blackened forelegs.
“Gave way” naturally conveys the forelegs bending under him.
It retains the monster’s rise from the abyss and temple-like collapse.
It preserves the weight shaking the earth and dust rising.
“Man” keeps the meaning while avoiding the stiffer “human.”
It preserves the Hunter’s former title and the butler’s relief.
“That’s enough” keeps his sense of satisfaction in natural speech.
It retains that half of Behemoth’s legs are unusable.
The pursuit clause is carried into H065, so its deletion avoids repetition.
It preserves both the inability to pursue Minwoo and the lives saved.
It retains his smile as he watches the shadow approach.
The impact and pain are carried through his flight like a cannonball.
SOL omits that his back breaks against the rock.
It retains the vomit, fading eyes, and organ fragments in the blood.
“Ears rang” changes the source’s muffled, blocked hearing.
It preserves the arsonist joke in spontaneous speech.
It keeps the profanity and the irritated “get lost” response.
BASE marks “go out” as the pun-bearing phrase; SOL removes that cue despite retaining the footnote.
The note is relocated to H137, where it still explains the wordplay.
“That changes things” keeps the shift in attitude.
The first-meeting setup is included in H077, avoiding a repeated sentence.
SOL drops “idol,” an important part of how Kim Hwajong viewed Taemin.
“Before long, he did” changes the prediction coming true into an unclear action by the man.
It keeps the long Great War and his becoming Taemin’s shadow.
The added reflection is sourced here and prepares for Taemin’s question in H081.
It naturally conveys Taemin answering Kim Hwajong’s uncertainty with a question.
“Anything you ask” preserves his willingness to do whatever Taemin requests.
The source says Taemin accepted Jungryong and Cheonwoo; SOL says they joined.
“That Peace Guild thing?” keeps the dismissive, casual tone.
It preserves the complaint about the name and the Ares suggestion.
It keeps Taemin accepting the suggestion and promising security in old age.
It retains his reluctance about office work and acceptance of the role.
It keeps the repeated request to call him hyung and the teasing complaint.
It preserves that Kim Hwajong never changed, as Taemin had said.
The source says his relationships grew distant; SOL makes Kim Hwajong himself the one growing distant.
It preserves his fiery temperament and constant swearing after peace arrived.
It keeps the child losing both parents and the decision to change.
The shortened ellipsis keeps the hesitant greeting.
It preserves the small funeral and the lonely four- or five-year-old.
It keeps the boy clinging to his grandfather and the sight’s effect on Kim Hwajong.
“Without hesitation” preserves his ready acceptance.
“Of the boy?” keeps the hesitant clarification.
The detail about Taemin living as if pursued is moved here from H099.
Its content is carried into H098, so deleting it avoids duplication.
The clipped fragments keep the required neatness, gentleness, and smile.
“Set a page … ablaze” preserves the image in idiomatic English.
It keeps the warning, concern, and affectionate reaction.
The glossary sense is picky eating; “be picky” can refer to preferences beyond food.
It preserves the gentle plea not to cry.
“The boy” accurately refers to the child who grows into a young man.
“At his side” implies physical proximity; the source says Kim Hwajong held his post.
The source says he stopped crying while thinking of his parents, not crying for them.
It keeps the moment Kim Hwajong sees traces of someone in the young man’s face.
The source refers to a Guild he said he would create, not a future plan phrased as a question.
It preserves the request for Kim Hwajong to serve as Guild Master.
The source explicitly asks what to name the Guild; SOL replaces the established term with “it.”
“I’m going to call it” preserves the decision to name it the Peace Guild.
The shorter ellipsis preserves the startled reaction.
“Displeased” naturally keeps the question about his unhappy expression.
It retains his hesitation amid many thoughts before he laughs.
It preserves his insincere-sounding praise of the name.
The founding and daily joy are carried into H118.
It carries forward the founding-day reflection and preserves the Guild’s growth and his Young Master’s change.
“Good days ahead” keeps his hopeful expectation.
It preserves his hope of staying beside the Young Master as he grows.
“Supposed to be” adds doubt; the source says today really was the best day of his life.
It preserves the reason he can laugh while dying.
It retains his question about what else the Young Master said.
“Tell you that” preserves the sense of wanting to say it before.
“Yes. That was it” naturally confirms the remembered words.
It keeps him raising his head through coughing and the mist in his fading vision.
It preserves the hope and fear still alive and leaving beyond the mist.
It keeps the trembling speech and bloodied lips.
It preserves the monster’s satisfaction as it opens its jaws.
“Across the ground” narrows the gust that sweeps in every direction.
It retains the flames, scattered limbs and blood, and rocks being drawn in.
“They” clearly refers to everything sucked in and keeps it spinning in Behemoth’s mouth.
The source calls it his final greeting; “farewell” changes that pragmatic cue.
“Touched his lips” keeps the faint smile in natural prose.
SOL adds that the voice spoke the name, which the source leaves unstated.
It preserves the burst of light turning the world white.
The footnote accurately explains the Korean verb’s “get lost” and flame “go out” meanings.
